Thus, avoiding a fatty diet and taking balance food, regular exercise and walking can keep the heart healthy."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Marked ‘S’ of the stem occurs in all higher and lower organisms—Explain it.","marks":3,"answer":"The figure "S" depicts the glycolysis stage of respiration process which occurs in all higher and lower organisms. It can be divided into two types, such as, aerobic and anaerobic. In both cases glycolysis is the common step. In glycolysis, a glucose molecule (C₆H₁₂O₆) is converted into two molecules of pyruvic acid (C₃H₄O₃). Nearly all living organisms (higher and lower organisms) carry out glycolysis as part of their metabolism. It takes place in the cytoplasm of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Four molecules of ATP (two ATP being used in the process) and two molecules of NADH + H⁺ are produced in this stage. In this process, no oxygen is required."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"What will be the effect on the living world in terms of ‘S’ if the mentioned process ‘P’ is interrupted? Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":""P" denotes photosynthesis in the stem. Conversely figure "S" represents cellular respiration. Although cellular respiration and photosynthesis evolved as independent processes, today they are interdependent. The products of photosynthesis, carbohydrates and oxygen gas, are used during cellular respiration. Likewise, the byproduct of cellular respiration, CO₂ gas, is used during photosynthesis. As they are interdependent; So, if photosynthesis is interrupted, as a result, cellular respiration would also be interrupted. Without this process; living world would face its extinction. This is analyzed below—
Photosynthesis is the process where glucose is formed by using Sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. On the other hand, the produced glucose in the photosynthetic process is oxidized to generate ATP and CO₂. For running the life process, thousands of biochemical reactions are going on in the living cells. All there reactions are run by bioenergy i.e. ATP. So, if photosynthesis do not take place, glucose would not be formed. consequently, the generation of ATP would be stopped as glucose would not be oxidized in the respiration process. As a result, all the physiological processes would be stopped and ultimately the plant or animal would become dead.
Again, CO₂ is required for the production of food. Green plants absorb CO₂ from the air and used it as a raw material in photosynthesis for manufacturing carbohydrate. During this process, O₂ is evolved as a by product. All living organisms depend for their food directly or indirectly on photosynthesis. When carbohydrate is utilized in respiration, CO₂ is evolved. Without this CO₂ photosynthesis cannot occur. Without photosynthesis there will deficiency of O₂ in environment and the environment will be polluted. As a result, the living organisms including animals will become extinct.
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Write down the chemical formula of pyruvic acid.","marks":1,"answer":"The chemical formula of pyruvic acid is C₃H₄O₃."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why Calvin cycle is called as C₃ pathway?","marks":2,"answer":"No light is directly required in the light independent phase of photosynthesis. In this phase, carbohydrates are produced by the reduction of CO₂ with the help of ATP, NADPH and H⁺. In green plants, three pathways of CO₂ reduction have been identified. One of them is Calvin cycle which is also called C₃ pathway. It is because the first compound produced here is a three-carbon compound."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the steps which are happened inside the mitochondria of the 1st reaction mentioned in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The first reaction of the stem signifies the aerobic respiration process.
The respiration process, which requires oxygen and produces CO₂, H₂O and a large amount of energy by oxidizing the respiratory materials. This process is completed in 4 steps—glycolysis, Acetyl Co-A formation, Kreb’s cycle and electron transport system. Among them, Kreb’s cycle and electron transport system are carried out in the mitochondria. These steps are discussed below:
Krebs' cycle: This stage occurs inside the mitochondria where Acetyl-CoA is used. During this stage 3NADH₂, 1FADH₂ and 1GTP molecules are produced from each molecule of Acetyl-CoA used with the evolution of 2CO₂ molecules. Thus 6 NADH₂, 2FADH₂ and 2GTP molecules are produced from 2 molecules of Acetyl-CoA used.
Electron transport system : In this process NADH+H⁺ and FADH₂ produced in glycolysis and Kreb's cycle are oxidised, and consequently ATP, water, electrons and protons are produced. The energy is released at the time of passing of electrons containing high-energy through the electron transport system. The energy is used in the formation of ATP. Electron transport system is carried out in mitochondria."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Discuss comparatively of the 1st and 2nd reaction mentioned in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The 1st and 2nd reactions of the stem are aerobic and anaerobic respiration respectively.
The process through which food materials (glucose) are oxidized with the help of oxygen to produce CO₂ and energy is called respiration. It is of two types – aerobic respiration and anaerobic respiration.
Aerobic respiration: The respiration process, which requires oxygen and produces CO₂, H₂O and a large amount of energy by oxidizing the respiratory materials. This process is completed in 4 steps – glycolysis, Acetyl Co-A formation, Kreb's cycle and electron transport system. Among them, Kreb's cycle and electron transport system are carried out in the mitochondria.
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂  Enzyme→ 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (686 KCal/mol)
Anaerobic respiration: The respiration which occurs in absence of oxygen, is called anaerobic respiration. In anaerobic respiration, respiratory substances being partially oxidized with the help of enzymes, produce different types of organic compounds (ethyl alcohol, lactic acid etc), CO₂ and small amount of energy. It consists of two stages, namely- glycolysis and incomplete reduction of Pyruvic Acid. Only in some microorganisms such as in bacteria, yeast etc. anaerobic respiration occurs.
C₆H₁₂O₆  Enzyme→ 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ + energy 56 Kcal/mole
These are the key features of aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
---"}]

Due to this, the rate of photosynthesis decreases at afternoon."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the cytoplasmic stages of the second process of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The second process mentioned in the stem is respiration. Glycolysis and Acetyl Co-A formation are the cytoplasmic stages of respiration. They are described below.
Glycolysis: Through many chemical reactions, a molecule of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is broken down into two molecules of pyruvic acid (C₃H₄O₃). Four molecules of ATP (two ATP is used) and two molecules of NADH+H⁺ are produced. As, in this process, no oxygen is required, it is the initial stage for both the aerobic and anaerobic respiration. It takes place in the cytoplasm of a cell.
Acetyl Co-A formation: This stage also takes place in the cytoplasm. Each molecule of pyruvic acid, produced in glycolysis, is transformed into a molecule of 2-carbon acetyl co-A, a molecule of CO₂ and a molecule of NADH+H⁺ (i.e. from two molecules of pyruvic acid two molecules of acetyl Co-enzyme-A, two molecules of CO₂ and two molecules of NADH+H⁺ are produced)."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"If the first process of the stem had not been completed. The living world would have extinct. Give your logic in favour of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"The first process mentioned in the stem is photosynthesis. If the process photosynthesis had not been completed, the living world would have extinct. My logic is given below.
The sun is the main source of all energy. Only green plants can transform solar energy into chemical energy and store as food through photosynthesis. No animal can produce their own food; they depend directly or indirectly on plants. Without photosynthesis, no food would be produced, leading to starvation and extinction of all animals. Also, photosynthesis releases oxygen. Without oxygen, aerobic respiration would stop, causing death of all aerobic organisms. The balance of CO₂ and O₂ in the atmosphere would be disrupted, making the environment uninhabitable.
---"}]

Here, P is carbon dioxide and Q is light. Deficiency or absence of these will interfere with the photosynthesis process. It is analyzed below.\nThe importance of light in photosynthesis is immense. For the production of carbohydrates from H₂O and CO₂, the source of required energy is light. Sunlight takes part in the development of chlorophyll. # Corrected Creative Questions
Photosynthesis process is divided into two stages. In the first stage ATP is produced and in the other stage CO₂ is reduced.

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called complex tissue?","marks":1,"answer":"The tissue composed of more than one type of cells is called complex tissue."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"How does temperature effect on photosynthesis?","marks":2,"answer":"Temperature as a factor plays a very important role in the process of photosynthesis. At a very low temperature (around 0°C) and a very high temperature (above 45°C), photosynthesis cannot be carried out. If temperature remains below 22°C or above 35°C, the rate of photosynthesis will decrease."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the first stage of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Light dependent phase is the first phase of photosynthesis. ATP is produced in this phase. The light dependent phase of photosynthesis is explained below.
Light is essential in the light dependent phase of photosynthesis. In this phase, solar energy is transformed into chemical energy. Through this process ATP (Adenosine triphosphate) and NADPH+H⁺ (reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate) are produced. This converted energy is stored in ATP. Chlorophyll plays a very important role in the production of ATP and NADPH+H⁺. Chlorophyll molecules absorb photons from light, and with the help of the energy obtained from the photon, ATP is formed through the addition of an inorganic phosphate with ADP. The process of the formation of ATP is called photophosphorylation. Oxygen, hydrogen and electrons are released through the hydrolysis of water with the help of sunlight and chlorophyll. The process is called the photolysis of water. ATP is produced through the process of photophosphorylation. The electrons reduce NADP, and produce NADPH+H⁺. These produced ATP and NADPH+H⁺ are called assimilatory power."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze a comparative study of two pathways of reduction of the related gas at the last stage of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Light independent phase is the last phase of photosynthesis. In green plants, C₃ cycle and C₄ cycle are the pathways of CO₂ reduction. The comparative analysis of the movements of the two cycles is given below.
C₃ cycle is commonly known as Calvin cycle. On the other hand, C₄ cycle is commonly known as Hatch and Slack pathway.
The C₃ cycle is present in all plants. On the other hand, the C₄ cycle is present only in C₄ plants.
First stable product in C₃ cycle is 3 phosphoglyceric acid. On the other hand, first stable product in C₄ cycle is Oxaloacetic acid.
The CO₂ acceptor in the C₃ cycle is ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate. On the other hand, the first CO₂ acceptor in the C₄ cycle is Phosphoenolpyruvate.
The first enzyme in C₃ cycle is ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase. On the other hand, the first enzyme in C₄ cycle is phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase.
The rate of photosynthesis of C₃ plants is low. On the other hand, the rate of photosynthesis of C₄ plants is high.
---"}]

| Stage of respiration | Substance produced | Used substance | Neat production of ATP |
|----------------------|-------------------|----------------|------------------------|

| | (ii) 2 x 2 = 4 molecules of FADH₂ | | (ii) 8 ATP |
| | (iii) 2 x 2 = 4 molecules of GTP | | (iii) 4 ATP |
Here, 1 molecule of NADH + H⁺ = 3 molecules of ATP
1 molecule of FADH₂ = 2 molecules of ATP
1 molecule of GTP = 1 molecule of ATP
In this way, 2 molecules of glucose produce a total of 48 molecules of ATP in the Krebs cycle."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The process of the stem is significant for the living world — Explain.","marks":4,"answer":"The process of the stem is the process of respiration. The process is very significant for living organisms as explained below.
All types of reactions and activities of plants and animals are conducted with the energy generated in the process of respiration. This process takes place 24 hours a day in plants and animals. Carbon dioxide released in respiration is used by plants for photosynthesis to produce sugars, the main food of organisms. This process helps plants absorb mineral salts, which indirectly supports plant growth and other biological processes. The energy required for plant and animal cell division and some accessory substances come from the process of respiration. So, this process also controls the physical growth of the organism. This process also helps in other biological functions of life by helping in the formation of various alkalis and organic acids. Some bacteria cannot survive in the presence of oxygen. Their only way of producing energy is through respiration. Moreover, the energy required for plant growth and development comes from the respiration process. CO₂ produced in the process of respiration participates in photosynthesis to produce food as well as produce O₂. This O₂ is essential for the survival of animals. Besides, the process also plays an indirect role in maintaining the balance of the environment, which is important for all living things.
So, from the above discussion it can be understood that the process of respiration is significant for living organisms.
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is biological coin?","marks":1,"answer":"The chemical component which stores energy and supplies energy for other reactions when necessary is called biological coin or energy coin."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is maize called C₄ plant?","marks":2,"answer":"Maize is called C₄ plants, as C₄ cycle takes place in this plant. The first stable substance formed in this pathway is 4 carbon based Oxaloacetic acid. So, this pathway is called C₄ pathway. And the plants where this cycle takes place are called C₄ plants."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the flow chart of ‘E’ production in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The reaction mention above indicate the aerobic respiration process. A lots of energy in the form of ATP is produced in this process. Here, E represents ATP. The production of ATP through aerobic reaction is generally divided into 4 stages:
i. Glycolysis: It takes place in the cytoplasm of a cell. Here, two molecules of Pyruvic acid (C₃H₄O₃) are produced from one molecule of Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆). Ten molecules of ATP are produced through this process from which two molecules are being used.
ii. Acetyl Co-A formation: This stage also takes place in cytoplasm. Each molecule of pyruvic acid, produced in glycolysis, is transformed into a molecule of 2-carbon acetyl Co-A, a molecule of CO₂ and a molecule of NADH₂. In the meantime 3 molecules of ATP are produced.
iii. Krebs cycle: All the reaction of this cycle occurs in mitochondria. In this cycle, from one molecule of acetyl Co-A, two molecules of CO₂, 3 molecules of NADH₂, 1 molecule of FADH₂ and 1 molecule of GTP are produced. 12 molecules of ATP are produced in this process.
iv. Electron Transport System: in this stage NADH₂, FADH₂, GTP produced in the above three stages are oxidized.
Thus, through aerobic respiration, one molecule of Glucose is completely oxidized through these steps and produce 38 molecules of ATP or energy in total."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The process in the stem is indirectly dependent on solar energy—Explain.","marks":4,"answer":"The chemical reaction mentioned in the stem is the aerobic respiration process. Aerobic respiration indirectly depends on the solar energy. The reasons are described below—
The main respiratory substance in aerobic respiration is glucose. Glucose is fully oxidized in the presence of oxygen and produces CO₂, water and ATP or energy. This process is divided into 4 stages. They are-Glycolysis, Acetyl Co-A formation, Krebs cycle and ETS. These four steps are completed only when the respiratory materials or glucose is produced. Without glucose this respiration process is not possible. During photosynthesis On the other hand plants produce glucose through the reaction of CO₂ and water only in the presence of sunlight. During photosynthesis the solar energy transformed into chemical energy and stored in the form of glucose. During respiration it is converted into energy or ATP.
From the above discussion, it is clear that without the presence of solar energy glucose cannot be produced. And without glucose aerobic respiration is not possible. Therefore, the process of the stem indirectly depends on the solar energy.
---"}]

The whole photosynthetic process is completed in two steps- the light dependent stage and the light independent stage.
In the presence of sunlight and chlorophylls, plants produce carbohydrates from CO₂ and H₂O and gives off O₂. Here, Sunlight is converted into chemical energy and ATP and NADPH₂ are produced. In the presence of light, an e⁻ is discharged from a chlorophyll molecule and reaches the same or another chlorophyll molecule. In this process, ATP is produced. Again, NADPH₂ is produced in an acyclic process. Photolysis of water occurs in the acyclic process, releasing oxygen. In the light independent stage, CO₂ is reduced by ATP and NADPH₂ and glucose is formed."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The process which happened in mentioned ‘Y’ is essential for living organism—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"The ‘Y’ in the stem is a mitochondria. And, the respiration process is took place in mitochondria. In addition, this particular process is essential for living organism. This is analyzed below-
In respiration process, food is broken down via a range of metabolic reaction, and energy is produced. CO₂ gas, is a by product of respiration reactions. This gas is used in photosynthesis by plants, where it is converted into simpler sugar at first. Again, the energy from respiration is used up in photosynthesis for making food and in minerals uptake process for plant growth. Also energy is required in cellular divisions which comes from respiration. It controls some physiological systems of plants including production of some organic acids to be used up in other biological processes of plants or animals. Respiration helps maintain the balance of CO₂ and O₂ in the air. Some bacteria cannot survive in the presence of O₂ and so they carry out anaerobic respiration.
So, respiration is essential for living organism.
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is water photolysis?","marks":1,"answer":"The process by which oxygen, hydrogen and electrons are released through hydrolysis of water with the help of sunlight and chlorophyll is known as photolysis of water."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"In living cells, preserving and releasing of energy is continue in cyclic order — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Through photosynthesis, plants store solar energy in carbohydrates as potential energy. The stored energy in the food cannot be directly used by the organisms for the maintenance of their life. During respiration, this potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (ATP) in the form of heat, which supplies the necessary energy for various physiological activities. The complex compounds in the bodies of living organisms, are broken down into simple compounds and later transformed into ATP. At normal temperature, the process of respiration occurs in the living organisms around the clock. So, in living cell, preserving and releasing of energy is continued in cyclic order."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"From 2 molecule glucose of the mentioned stem how many molecules of 'B' will produce? Calculate.","marks":3,"answer":"The reaction mentioned in the stem is aerobic respiration. Here, ‘B’ is ATP. Production of ATP from 2 molecule glucose through a chart is shown below - Energy obtained from aerobic respiration:
| Stage of respiration | Substance produced | Used substance | Neat product |
|----------------------|-------------------|----------------|--------------|
| Glycolysis | 2 molecules pyruvic acid, 2 molecules NADH+H⁺, 4 molecules ATP | 2 molecules ATP | 6 ATP |
| Acetyl Co-A | 2 molecules acetyl Co-A, 2 molecules CO₂, 2 molecules NADH+H⁺ | 2 molecules pyruvic acid | 2 molecules CO₂, 6 ATP |
| Kreb’s Cycle | 4 molecules CO₂, 6 molecules NADH+H⁺, 2 molecules FADH₂, 2 molecules GTP | 2 molecules acetyl Co-A | 4 molecules CO₂, 18 ATP, 4 ATP, 2 ATP |
| Total | | | 38 ATP (net total ATP) + 6 molecules CO₂ |
1 molecule NADH + H⁺ or NADH₂ = 3 molecules ATP
1 molecule FADH₂ = 2 molecules ATP
1 molecule GTP = 1 molecules ATP
In aerobic respiration, 1 molecule of glucose is completely oxidized to produce 38 ATP.
So, in aerobic respiration, 2 molecule of glucose is completely oxidized to produce (38 × 2) = 76 ATP."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Mentioned reaction play an important role in existence of organisms — Analyze with logic.","marks":4,"answer":"The reaction mentioned in the stem is respiration. Respiration is very important for the survival of an organism. Development, reproduction, locomotion, differentiation of a living organism require a constant input of energy. The prime source of this energy is sun. Green plants can deposit the solar energy as chemical energy in the form of carbohydrates within them through photosynthesis. However, living organisms can not use these foods directly. Respiration is the sole biological event that helps the organisms to release stored energy from food. The stored internal potential energy is converted into heat energy and can be used to conduct every kinds of physicochemical reactions of the said organism. Energy can also be released from fats, proteins, organic acids through respiration. Usually complex food molecules are oxidized into a simpler version through respiration to release energy. This energy helps to conduct all biological event within a living organism.
Therefore, it can be stated that respiration plays an important role in existence of organisms.
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called complex tissue?","marks":1,"answer":"The permanent tissue formed by the combination of different types of cells is called complex tissue."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is ATP called rechargeable battery? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"ATP is the biological currency or energy currency of the organism. When chemical bonds of ATP are broken, energy is released, with which every biological function of life is carried out. ATP is formed by rejoining the broken fragments through phosphorylation by the energy released from the oxidation of the food consumed by the organism. It breaks down again when energy is needed. Then it takes energy from the food and rejoins. Hence it is called rechargeable battery."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the process of occurrence of reaction no. (i) of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The stem's (i) reaction is shown to be anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen. Anaerobic respiration occurs in two steps. The two steps are—
Step 1: Incomplete oxidation of glucose : From one molecule of glucose, two molecules of pyruvic acid, four molecules of ATP (two of them already used) and two molecules of NADH+H⁺ are produced. This process looks similar to glycolysis in aerobic respiration. However, it is considered that the oxidation of glucose here is incomplete because the pyruvic acid that is produced here is reduced in the next stage.
Step 2: Reduction of pyruvic acid : With the help of enzymes in the cytoplasm, pyruvic acid is reduced to CO₂ and ethyl alcohol, or only lactic acid. In this case NAD (NADH+H⁺), which is reduced in glycolysis, releases electron, proton and energy after oxidization and these are used to produce lactic acid and in some cases ethanol from pyruvic acid. On the other hand, oxidative phosphorylation does not take place because of the absence of oxygen. So, in anaerobic respiration, only two molecules of ATP are produced from the glycolysis of glucose."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"In the reaction no. (ii) of the stem, E-independent phase occurs in different ways in different plants—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"In the stem, the E of reaction (ii) is light and the reaction is of photosynthesis process. The light independent or dark phase of photosynthesis takes place in different plants in different ways. It is analyzed below — The photosynthesis process of plants that does not require direct light is called light independent phase. Carbon dioxide is reduced to carbohydrates in the light independent phase with the help of ATP, NADPH+H⁺ and H⁺ produced mainly in the light dependent phase. Mainly in green plants, three cycles have been discovered for the reduction of carbon dioxide, the Calvin cycle, the Hatch and Slack cycle, and the Crassulacean acid metabolism cycle. The Calvin cycle of carbon-dioxide assimilation occurs in most plants. They are called C₃ plants as the first stable product produced in this process is 3-carbon phosphoglyceric acid. Calvin cycle is completed in most herbaceous plants especially dicotyledonous plants. The second pathway of carbon dioxide assimilation is Hatch and Slack cycles which produce oxaloacetic acid containing 4-carbon as the first stable product. That is why the cycle is called C₄ cycle. Commonly, C₄ occurs in corn, grass like plants, Mutha grass, amaranthus, and monocots. And the third cycle is the Crassulacean acid metabolism cycle which is followed by some plants for adaptation to dry environment. The first stable substance in this cycle is malic acid which has four carbons. Stonecrops and some thorny plants such as Pineapple, Phonimansa open their stomata at night in light deficiency and fix carbon inside them.
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Bioenergetics?","marks":1,"answer":"Bioenergetics is concerned with the energy involved in making and breaking of chemical bonds in the molecules found in biological organisms."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Photosynthesis does not occur equally in all visible spectrum—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The photosynthesis process require sunlight. But, plants do not make equal use of all the wavelengths present in the full range of visible light. Red, blue, orange and purple portions of the visible spectrum function better than that of green and yellow in the process of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis, generally, is carried out well with light of wave length between 400nm-480nm and 680 nm. In other wavelength of light, the rate of photosynthesis is not good enough."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How many ATP's are formed from 1 molecule of glucose in the reaction (ii) in stem? Show with calculation.","marks":3,"answer":"The reaction (ii) is aerobic respiration. In this process, 1 molecule of glucose produces 38 ATP molecules. The calculation is:
- Glycolysis: 2 ATP (net) + 2 NADH₂ → 6 ATP (total 8 ATP)
- Acetyl Co-A formation: 2 NADH₂ → 6 ATP
- Krebs cycle: 6 NADH₂ → 18 ATP, 2 FADH₂ → 4 ATP, 2 GTP → 2 ATP
- Total: 8+6+18+4+2 = 38 ATP"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze comparative differences between process (i) and (ii) in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Process (i) is photosynthesis and process (ii) is respiration. Differences:
- Photosynthesis uses CO₂ and H₂O to produce glucose and O₂ using sunlight. Respiration uses glucose and O₂ to produce CO₂, H₂O and energy.
- Photosynthesis occurs only in green plants and some bacteria. Respiration occurs in all living organisms.
- Photosynthesis stores solar energy as chemical energy in glucose. Respiration releases that stored energy as ATP.
- Photosynthesis is an anabolic process. Respiration is a catabolic process.
- Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts. Respiration occurs in cytoplasm and mitochondria.
---"}]

Explain it.","marks":2,"answer":"Chlorophyll is present in chloroplasts in leaves. A direct relationship exists between the rate of photosynthesis and the chlorophyll. Because only chlorophyll located in chloroplast takes light energy and causes photosynthesis. When the chlorophyll content in the leaves is normal, the rate of photosynthesis increases. However, if there is too much chlorophyll or chloroplast in the cell, there is a lack of enzymes and the rate of photosynthesis decreases."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the effects of three factors that externally influence the process mentioned in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The process mentioned in stem is aerobic respiration. The effect of three external factors — temperature, oxygen and water — on the process of respiration is explained below.
Temperature: Respiration rate decreases at temperatures below 20°C and above 45°C. The best temperature for respiration is 20°C to 45 °C.
Oxygen: During respiration, pyruvic acid is oxidized to produce CO₂ and H₂O. Therefore, in the absence of oxygen, respiration cannot continue at all.
Water: Moderate water supply keeps respiration normal. But in the presence of too little or too much water, the respiration process is disturbed."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"How does the stem mentioned process occur in yeast? Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"The process of the stem is respiration. Respiration in yeast occurs in the absence of oxygen, this type of respiration is called anaerobic respiration. Through respiration, the respiratory substances are partially oxidized by an intermediate enzyme to produce various organic compounds (ethyl alcohol, lactic acid, etc.), CO₂ and a small amount of energy. The reaction of respiration is as follows:
C₆H₁₂O₆  Enzyme→ 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ + Energy Glucose Ethyl alcohol
The process of respiration is done in two steps. Namely-
Step-1: Incomplete oxidation of glucose: In this step, two molecules of pyruvic acid, four molecules of ATP and two molecules of NADH + H⁺ are produced from one molecule of glucose.
Step-2: Incomplete reduction of pyruvic acid: Under the action of enzymes located in the cytoplasm, pyruvic acid is decomposed to produce CO₂ and ethyl alcohol or just lactic acid.
---"}]
